after: A float is a box that sits to one side while nearby text wraps beside it. This can be useful for a small picture inside a story.
`display: flow-root` goes on the parent story. It creates a separate block layout area that includes its floats when the parent’s height is worked out. That helps the story box surround the map.
`clear: left` makes the next section start below earlier left floats. If the map grows taller, the cleared section moves farther down. It stays below the map.

Use a float for a picture with text flowing around it. Flex or grid is usually a clearer choice for larger page layouts. Here, `left` means the physical left side; it does not switch automatically for right-to-left writing.
